Posted May 16, 2002
Analysis by Richard Cowan

The DEAland government is having problems with its prohibitionist propaganda. First, Drug Czar Walters has announced that the government's billion dollar lying campaign is not fooling the kids. In fact, it may even be counterproductive and encourage marijuana use among the targeted groups. Surprise! Surprise!

Has Walters learned anything from this? No. In fact, he is planning a new ad campaign, and this is what he says about it:

" It's also going to provide more direct messages about the real threats We are going to turn and look more directly at marijuana. "

That is just about as explicit as is possible. The Drug War is really about cannabis.
See

Then there is the matter of medical cannabis: The Down To Seeds And Stems Again Blues.

The prohibitionist party line is that there needs to be scientific research to determine whether cannabis really has medical value. The National Institute on Drug Abuse is supposed to be the scientific agency that oversees this process.
See

For example, NIDA has been growing cannabis at the University of Mississippi for " research " since the 1970s. It controls all access to cannabis for medical research, and consequently they are able to delay or block any research that they think may challenge the party line.

Of course, they pretend to be " scientists, " but a controversy over a California study is showing them up as the political hacks and quacks that they really are. NIDA more or less had to approve this study because it was being sponsored by San Mateo County in California.Of course, they were able to delay the study for several years before giving it the green light and Mississippi schwag last year.
From four years ago see
San Mateo County Plans Research On Medical Marijuana;
They May Learn More Than They Expect

Now is it 2002. How time flies when you're not in pain!

But there is a problem getting people to enroll in the study because the word is out that the NIDA weed is of such low quality. That is not a surprise to those of us who know the seven remaining legal users who are given 300 joints a month under the so-called " Compassionate Access Investigative New Drug " program.
See

So far, only 10 people are taking part in San Mateo the study, which was designed for 60, because the weed is loaded with seeds and stems! Consequently, there have been a number of stories in the media about the problems, and this has drawn a very interesting response from a NIDA official in charge of lying to the media, Steve Gust, " the special assistant to the director of NIDA. " Very special indeed!

Gust claims that " the marijuana that we provide and produce is almost entirely free of stems and seeds. "

My friend Dr. Ethan Russo, a Montana neurologist, who is also the editor of the Journal of Cannabis Therapeutics, has had his own experiences with NIDA. He knows that they lie.
See
NIDA Refuses To Sell 400 Grams of Medical Marijuana For FDA Approved Migraine Research. Giving A Prohibitionist Propaganda Organization A Veto on Medical Research.

Russo got one of the seven legal patients to unroll three of the Mississippi joints and he took a picture of it, and posted it on the web. Even I was shocked, and that is pretty hard to do these days.
See http://www.freedomtoexhale.com/debris.jpg

Now remember that NIDA is supposed to be a scientific agency, just looking for the facts, ma am.

So consider this for scientific attitude: Gust, " the special assistant to the director of NIDA, " told the Arizona Republic that groups like NORML are looking for something to blame if the results of the studies show it has little medicinal value. " Then they can say the marijuana isn't of sufficient quality. "

He lies about the quality of the cannabis they are providing and then attacks the motives of those who raise questions about it. Ah, yes, the scientific method!

However, Gust may also be having some problems as a propagandist. At one point he forgot to lie.

In response to complaints that the Mississippi schwag is too low in THC he told the San Francisco Chronicle that the government's marijuana tests at almost the same level of potency as " the average marijuana that is seized by the federal Drug Enforcement Administration, which is about 4 to 5 percent. "

But how is that possible?

We are always being told that marijuana today is so much more potent -- as much as 20% THC --than what we smoked " back in the sixties when everyone thought that it was harmless. "
See

The problem with lying is that it is so difficult to remember what lies you are supposed to tell.

The truth is not just " out there. " It is right here for anyone to see.

So much of what I deal with on MarijuanaNews.com really is hard to imagine. That is why I have brought these items together here. The war on cannabis is a war on truth and freedom. Can anyone be neutral?
See
